answers.reason: Heracleopolis Magna is the Egyptian settlement at Ihnasiyyah al Madinah; Hierapolis in COL 4:13 is in Phrygia.
Heracleopolis Parva is the Egyptian settlement identified here with Tell Belim; Hierapolis in COL 4:13 is in Phrygia.
Herod’s palace in Jerusalem is a royal palace, whereas both candidates denote sanctuary rooms.
The record explicitly identifies Hilakku with Cilicia. Lakkum is a settlement on Naphtali’s boundary in JOS 19:33.
Janua is identified with Yamun, a different settlement from both Khirbet Yanun (JOS 16:6–7) and Yanouh (2KI 15:29). None of the other candidates matches its location or identity.
Kumidi at Kamid el Loz is a settlement in the Beqaa Valley. It is distinct from the Midian region east of Aqaba and Middin in Judah (JOS 15:61).
Laash is located near Hamath in Syria. The candidates identify other places, including Lasha at Callirrhoe and Laish/Dan farther south; spelling similarity does not establish identity.
Madiama is identified with Al Bad in northwestern Arabia. None of the candidates denotes that settlement; Media is a separate region despite the similar name.
Magdalsenna is identified with Khirbat al Beiyudat in the Jordan Valley. Magdala/Magadan and the other candidates denote different settlements.

Magdolum at Tell el Herr likely corresponds to the Egyptian Migdol of JER 44:1 and 46:14. However, both migdol and migdol-2 explicitly identify Tell el Herr, and migdol-3 aliases the latter, so the supplied data does not establish exactly one target.
